createTable.remarks: What to show -- at most one row per owning entity (PROVIDER_PROFILE or ADVERTISEMENT), holding phone/telegram/viber. No DB-level FK to provider_profile/advertisement, same entity_type+entity_id convention audit_log already uses -- resolved only via ContactPort, never a SQL join. An ADVERTISEMENT row is an optional per-listing override of the owner's PROVIDER_PROFILE row; fallback resolution lives in marketplace-orchestrator.

column.name: entity_type
column.remarks: Owning entity type (EntityType: PROVIDER_PROFILE or ADVERTISEMENT). No FK -- resolved via ContactPort, not a join

column.name: entity_id
column.remarks: ID of the owning entity. References provider_profile(id) or advertisement(id) depending on entity_type, no FK

createTable.remarks: Where/how many clicked -- append-only event log, one row per reveal, same immutable-table shape as audit_log (never updated, only inserted). Each channel reveals and counts independently of the others.

column.name: entity_type
column.remarks: Type of entity whose contact was revealed (EntityType: PROVIDER_PROFILE or ADVERTISEMENT). No FK

column.name: entity_id
column.remarks: ID of the entity whose contact was revealed

column.name: channel
column.remarks: Which contact channel was revealed/clicked -- PHONE / TELEGRAM / VIBER (ContactChannel). Each channel reveals and counts independently of the others

column.name: viewer_id
column.remarks: Acting user id if authenticated, null for anonymous reveals. References user_information(id), no FK

column.name: created_at
column.remarks: Reveal timestamp. Immutable write-only table (never updated, only inserted), same shape as audit_log
